conclusion: In German men, HLA-DRB1*15:01 was less common among long-lived men (10%) than among younger controls (15%), so men carrying it had lower odds of reaching extreme old age (odds ratio 0.64). The same direction was seen in UK Biobank and, without reaching significance, in Danish men.
In German women, HLA-DRB1*15:01 showed no substantial decrease among long-lived women (14%); the association reached significance in men only.
HLA-B*57:01 was less frequent in European centenarians than in controls of the same origin (odds ratio about 0.68), across four national cohorts. It was measured through its tag SNP, rs2395029-G.
In a Dutch study, HLA-A*02:01 was one of six HLA alleles that lowered the likelihood of becoming a cognitively healthy centenarian (odds ratios 0.59 to 0.74 across the six). The study is a preprint.
